newsitem.title: USA: Rubin optimistic on getting tax deal with Congress.
newsitem.headline: Rubin optimistic on getting tax deal with Congress.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin reiterated his opposition on Tuesday to much of the tax plan proposed by House Ways and Means Chairman Bill Archer, but voiced optimism that the differences can be worked out.

"I think what he has created is a package that in almost every component has moved away from helping middle and lower income people and toward helping more affluent people," Rubin told public television's NewsHour with Jim Lehrer program.
He ticked off a number of areas where the administration disagrees with the Texas Republican's plan.
Neverthless, Rubin voiced optimism that the Clinton administration can reach agreement with Congress on a tax package.
"I'd like to be optimistic and think that we can work that out," he said, adding, "We all have to work together in a constructive spirit."
